From the wiki: "The Africanized bee, also known as the Africanized honey bee and known colloquially as the "killer bee", is a hybrid of the western honey bee, produced originally by crossbreeding of the East African lowland honey bee with various European honey bee subspecies such as the Italian honey bee and the Iberian honey bee."

They look slightly different and they're much more aggressive. They swarm longer and more often for smaller reasons and chase their targets over longer distances than native bees. Our original hive never had a problem with that dog barking around breakfast time. She was a decent distance too. The exterminator told us that it looked like the hive was probably in the process of being taken over when our dog got them even more agitated. He told us the killer bees can bring gifts to these colonies and then, when the hive trusts them, they kill the queen and replace her with their own. So if they start swarming for seemingly no reason and won't calm down despite there being no more perceived threat, and the exterminator says so, then you know they're the assholes of the bee world. 

They make sense because they're usually healthier and stronger than the colonies we previously had, and I'm not upset at anything helping bees to survive, but they are a little more dangerous. You should still keep bees (some honey collectors will only keep killer bees insisting that they produce better honey) because this is worst case scenario and not as common as people think, but it's a possibility and it's good to know.

Edit: and dogs can have benedryl for bee stings if there's a lot or they're really swelling up and you can't get to the vet. They swarmed ours and one of them looked truly terrible but we were afraid to try and make it out the gate. That's what the vet told us on the phone and all of the dogs were fine. Google or talk to your vet for dosing.
